597a44f0dab93e18.question: What does the customer want, and has the bank promised anything so far?

answer.answer: The customer wants back the interest they believe they lost, about £43.20. They say the rate on their Harbourline Easy Saver fell from 3.1% to 1.6% in July without any letter or email, and that they would have moved their money if they had known. The file records no promise or commitment from the bank. The only note says the customer's email bounced in rate change notice batch 06/2026, that no letter was sent instead, and that this is the first contact. Nothing in the file shows the customer has been offered or told anything about an outcome or redress. Those decisions rest with an authorised handler.

45406e353c78fcfd.question: What happened, in date order, and what is still unknown?

answer.answer: In date order: in July the Easy Saver rate fell from 3.1% to 1.6%. The customer says they never received a letter or email about it. Note_1 records that rate change notice batch 06/2026 was sent, but the customer's email bounced and no letter was sent instead. The complaint was received by web form on 2026-10-08, and the handler logged it the same day as a first contact. Still unknown: the exact date of the rate change and of the notice batch; how much notice was intended; whether the customer's email address on file was correct; how the £43.20 figure was calculated and whether it has been checked against the Q3 statement; and whether other customers' emails also bounced without a letter being sent.

c2427ef55851b423.question: Which policy rules decide this case, and what do they require the handler to do?

answer.answer: No clause specifically covers savings rate-change notices; the file has no savings notice rule (LND-5 covers mortgages only). Relevant rules: CH-1 makes this a complaint (dissatisfaction plus alleged loss). CH-6 suggests Low severity (loss under £100). CH-7 requires one root cause; Communication failure looks closest, since the email bounced with no letter fallback. No ESC-1 trigger appears, so the handler resolves it themselves. CH-2 requires logging and written acknowledgement within 3 business days; CH-4 requires a Final Response within 8 weeks. CH-8/RED-5: an authorised person decides uphold and redress; RED-1/RED-2 set the redress principle. CH-9 requires a full record. Whether the batch issue affected other customers is not in the file.
